failedGate: B1: Basketball credibility; the split-role turnover component lacks stable historical support. This prerequisite experiment cannot itself pass B1 or B2.
hypothesis: Limited prior exposure makes transported player turnover rates noisy. Minute-dependent shrinkage toward the prior league rate improves team turnover accounting without changing shooting or passing responsibilities.
formula: weight = priorMinutes / (priorMinutes + kMinutes); turnoverRate = weight * priorTurnoverRate + (1-weight) * priorLeagueTurnoverRate. kMinutes=0 returns the original input exactly. Existing fallback players are unchanged.
fixedInputs: Use the frozen team-study rows, previous league rates, actual target-minute weights, prior shot/assist rates, eligibility and explicit league fallback without alteration. No target TOV enters predictions.
cohort: Use only original team-study common support: every original scenario evaluated. Freeze row membership before shrinkage. New unsupported cases invalidate the affected configuration; never drop a row to improve it.
selection: Minimum equal-team training RMSE among configurations supported on every training row; exact ties choose smaller kMinutes. Include kMinutes=0. Freeze a separate selection artifact before any new later-period candidate prediction. No selection by high-coverage subset or later results.
comparison: Reuse team-study equal-team errors and paired MSE normal95 intervals clustered by target season. Evaluate only the selected configuration in later years, against both unchanged baselines; report league and high-coverage results too.
proceedRules: Selected kMinutes is positive and every originally common-support row remains supported.
Selected training RMSE is no higher than unchanged shot-only training RMSE.
On all later teams, selected RMSE is at least 2% lower than EACH of shot-only and unshrunk split-role, and EACH paired MSE interval upper bound is below zero.
On later teams with at least90% prior-minute coverage, selected RMSE is no higher than EITHER unchanged baseline. Report uncertainty without claiming subgroup significance.
failureAction: Any failed or unmeasurable proceed rule rejects candidate1 at the component gate. Stop this mechanism; no grid expansion, alternative shrinkage target, subset rescue or second later-period selection. Keep live balance. Candidate2 remains a separate budgeted decision.
successAction: Proceed only to complete-candidate integration assessment. Do not claim roster, difficulty, fun or release acceptance. No automatic promotion or measurement of fresh families.
limits: This counts as one of two scorecard candidate mechanisms, including rejection at this cheap prerequisite gate.
Minutes are a reliability proxy, not identified sampling variance. Shrinking toward league can erase real role differences.
Later years were already exposed in previous studies. This is selection-isolated evaluation, not fresh validation.
Uncapped season-aggregate rotations are not five-player units. Target minutes are observed; this is not a preseason forecast.
No new defense, spacing, coach, reserve, efficiency, score or win parameters; no old-era turnover imputation or changed peaks.
Team-only turnovers, historical missingness and a complete game integration remain unresolved. Better error cannot substitute for scorecard gates.
